Cowboys' James Houston could be playing his way into a new deal

He certainly deserves it.
ByJess Haynie|Nov 26, 2026, 8:00 AM EST
Add us as a preferred source
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 3:19
Instaread

It took a while for James Houston to break through early-season agendas and bureaucracy, but now he's emerged as one of the Cowboys' best pass rushers. He's also one of their unrestricted free agents in 2027, and the fifth-year veteran is making a case for a new contract.

Dallas started the year with other mouths to feed among their outside linebackers. They'd traded for veteran Rashan Gary, then added Von Miller shortly before the season. They also had rookie Malachi Lawrence and second-year prospect Donovan Ezeiruaku, who needed playing time to develop.

But after 11 games, those four players have just five total sacks combined. Meanwhile, in just four games of meaningful playing time, Houston has already accumulated 3.5 sacks. He is already second on the team behind Quinnen Williams' eight sacks, part of a monster season from Dallas' elite DT.

James Houston has proven his value before 2026

This isn't exactly a shocker.

Last season, Houston was second with 5.5 sacks behind only Jadeveon Clowney. He's proven two years in a row that even when the defense has overall struggled, his individual pass-rushing ability comes through when you get him on the field.

We don't know what the 2027 Cowboys defense will look like, or who will be running it. But a guy like Houston would be very valuable whether Dallas goes into another transition phase or just looks to build on the current foundation.

The Cowboys are going to be wary of putting "progress stoppers" in front of Lawrence and Ezeiruaku, and that's not unwise. But this defense needs to make some serious strides as a whole for Dallas to return to playoff contention, so the focus may need to shift to simply fielding the best possible unit and finding other ways to develop your younger prospects.

Houston's next deal may follow Dorance Armstrong's second contract

Back in 2022, Dallas had Dorance Armstrong coming off his rookie deal and a career-high five sacks. After three low years, he shined in 2021 after Dan Quinn's first season as defensive coordinator, and with rookie sensation Micah Parsons drawing so much attention.

Armstrong got a two-year, $12 million extension and rewarded the Cowboys with 15.5 sacks from 2022-2023. He followed Quinn to Washington in 2024, but Dallas had zero regrets about what they got from him in those final years.

Houston could be in line for a similar deal. For a player who's never even made $2 milliion in a single season, it'd be an impressive raise. And having just turned 28 about a week ago, plus having relatively low NFL mileage, Houston should have at least a couple of quality years left.

Armstrong was a bit younger (25 when Dallas gave him the second contract. But he'd also only given them one year of solid production, while Houston is looking ready to make it two consecutive years. So that may help mitigate any risk concerns about his age.

We'll how the rest of 2026 goes and what it means for James Houston's eventual free agent stock. But if the last four weeks are any indication, he's trending upward and building momentum at the right time. A strong finish could make him a significant figure in Dallas' next offseason.
